name: Spherical Harmonics

# Spherical Harmonics
Also called: Spherical Harmonic Volumetric Rendering
## Overview
Spherical Harmonics (SH) provide a complete basis of functions mapping the unit sphere $S^2$ to the complex numbers $\mathbb{C}$, used to represent directional functions like radiance in volumetric rendering [S1, unofficial]. Unlike Spherical Gaussians (SGs), SHs constitute a fixed, non-learnable basis, which simplifies implementation by removing the need for optimization of basis parameters [S1, unofficial].
## Shared principles
The method expands directional signals (such as lighting or view-dependent appearance) into a series of orthogonal basis functions defined on the sphere [S2, unofficial]. The basis is indexed by a degree $\ell \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{0\}$ and an order $m \in \{-\ell, \dots, \ell\}$ [S1, unofficial].
### Complex Basis Definition
The complex [spherical harmonic basis](#4390-spherical-harmonics-encoder.md) function $Y_\ell^m(\theta, \phi)$ is defined as [S1, unofficial]:
$$Y_\ell^m(\theta, \phi) = \sqrt{\frac{2\ell + 1}{4\pi} \frac{(\ell - m)!}{(\ell + m)!}} P_\ell^m(\cos \theta) e^{im\phi}$$
where $\theta$ is the polar angle (inclination), $\phi$ is the azimuthal angle, and $P_\ell^m$ are the associated Legendre polynomials [S1, unofficial].
### Real-Valued Basis Construction
For rendering applications, a real-valued basis $Y_\ell^m: S^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ is constructed from the complex analogue to ensure real-valued coefficients and outputs [S1, unofficial]. The mapping is defined as:
$$Y_\ell^m = \begin{cases} \sqrt{2} \cdot (-1)^m \cdot \text{Im}[Y_\ell^{|m|}] & \text{if } m < 0 \\ Y_\ell^0 & \text{if } m = 0 \\ \sqrt{2} \cdot (-1)^m \cdot \text{Re}[Y_\ell^m] & \text{if } m > 0 \end{cases}$$ [S1, unofficial].
### Basis Size and Truncation
The total number of basis functions for a maximum degree $L$ is $(L+1)^2$ [G]. Common truncations include SH-9 (Degree $L=2$, 9 coefficients), SH-16 (Degree $L=3$, 16 coefficients), and SH-25 (Degree $L=4$, 25 coefficients) [S1, unofficial]. Empirical ablation on the NeRF-synthetic dataset indicates that switching between max degree 3 (SH-16) and 4 (SH-25) yields negligible differences in metrics (PSNR, SSIM) or visual quality [S1, unofficial].
## Subtopics

### [Spherical Harmonic Volume Shading](5946-spherical-harmonic-volume-shading.md)
Applies SH to encode view-dependent shading within the volume.

### [Ray Tracing Backward Pass](5966-ray-tracing-backward-pass.md)
Uses SH for differentiable rendering gradients.

### H-Basis Encoding
A basis used to encode a hemispherical signal, requiring fewer coefficients to achieve the same quality as 3rd order spherical harmonics [S3, unofficial]. A coordinate system local to the surface is required to orient the hemisphere, commonly utilizing a tangent frame resulting from uv-parameterization [S3, unofficial]. If encoded in textures, the texture needs sufficient resolution to adapt to changes in the underlying tangent space [S3, unofficial]. If two triangles cover the same texel and have significantly different tangents, it leads to a lack of precision in the reconstructed signal [S3, unofficial].

## Background
Spherical Harmonics are a standard tool in computer graphics for representing spherical functions, originating from physics and mathematics [S2, unofficial]. In the context of neural volume rendering, SHs were adopted in PlenOctrees to compactly represent the directional radiance field, allowing for real-time rendering of Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) [S1, unofficial]. The specific implementation details and ablation studies regarding SH vs. SG in this context are documented in the PlenOctrees paper [S1, unofficial].
